Battleships Forever was probably just named for the boardgame, but has nothing to do with it.

It's unlike most RTS games, which revolve around resource management and reaction speed. BF has no resources but the handful of ships you picked for the mission, and you maneuver them to positions to take advantage of an enemy's weakpoint or to cover one of your own.

For example, you decided to pick up the mighty Cronus, a battleship with massive forward beams that prioritize on damage, piercing through resistances, and have ridiculous range. Problem is, it turns as well as a turtle and has a single laser that can protect its ass, so if something gets behind it, it's screwed.

So you decide to pack a couple Zelus to defend it. Imagine a bat with a gatling gun and you got a Zelus. You stick one towards each side of your Cronus, let him do the heavy lifting while they flank anyone that decides to get close and rip them to shreds.

The game is quite fun, but hasn't been supported for a long time (which is why the last two missions aren't available). Comes with a ship creating program so you can make your own. There are tons on the internet for you to try. People have made entire fleets of custom made ships. It used to have a massive cult following it, but not anymore.
